The top-level code consists entirely of: standard metadata variable definitions (`pkgbase`, `pkgver`, `depends`, etc.), array definitions for `source` (URLs from mozilla.org, not downloaded during sourcing), and two `for` loops. The first loop iterates over the hardcoded `_languages` array to append to `pkgname`/`source` arrays and uses `eval` to dynamically generate per-language `package_*()` functions — a well-known AUR i18n pattern. The second loop builds the `noextract` array from the already-constructed `source` array.

No top-level code performs network requests, downloads, file exfiltration, or executes untrusted payloads. The `eval` uses only hardcoded locale strings (e.g., `ach "Acholi"`) from the PKGBUILD itself, not external/user-controlled input. The `_url` variable references `archive.mozilla.org` (the expected upstream) but is only assigned as a string, never downloaded, during this step. No obfuscated, base64-encoded, or otherwise suspicious code appears at the top level.</summary>

No genuinely malicious behavior exists in the global scope code executed by `makepkg --printsrcinfo`.</summary>
